chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Abu Hammam from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Fasting the Day of Arafah is equivalent to a year [of fasting], and he said: Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) did not fast it, and Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) fasted it.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting on the Day of Arafah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the immense spiritual merit of fasting on the Day of Arafah, equating it to a full year of worship, a status particularly emphasized for those not performing Hajj. The specific mention of Imam al-Husayn fasting while Imam al-Hasan did not reflects the scholarly discussion on whether this was a matter of personal preference (khiyar) or a subtle legal distinction (khilaf) in their respective eras, underscoring the flexibility in the application of this highly rewarded sunnah.
